decisions.reason: The Definition explicitly distinguishes a canonical map (pullback equality) from a canonical transformation (diffeomorphism) and a local transformation (local diffeomorphism). The imported smooth definition has the same pullback equality and separately conditions its three terms on diffeomorphism, local diffeomorphism, or embedding. Smooth-case agreement does not identify every canonical map with an embedding. The polar covering counterexample satisfies the map definition and violates no claimed injectivity.

Step 2.1 cites F3 for the equality omega(X_f,X_g)={f,g} although the finite-regularity definition delegates that equality to this proposition. The intervening matrix computation already proves the equality independently, so this is a nonfatal circular presentation rather than a missing mathematical argument. Reordered the computation to start with omega(X_f,X_g), reduce it using J^T=-J and J^2=-I, and only then identify the result with the defined coordinate bracket. Field existence, uniqueness, equations and C^1 regularity remain valid; Statement unchanged.

Remarks only, no Statement or Definition changed.

The title covers global generators while the proof explicitly handles only second kind. This is nonfatal proof scope: a first-kind generator is impossible even locally, since Q=theta+k would make the relation I=S_theta(theta,Q) independent of the varying input momentum I. Added that elementary contradiction as step 4.1, preserving the title and all original Statement clauses. Also corrected F1 to require a surjective local diffeomorphism for injective pullback; pi has exactly this hypothesis. Checked descended forms, loop non-exactness, and the periodic integration constant c(theta)=hat S(theta,0) in the valid second-kind proof.

F2 speaks of a canonical map, which the finite-regularity definition defines by pullback equality without global injectivity. Clause 1 of the cited matrix-test proposition proves exactly that equality iff D Psi^T J D Psi=J; clause 2 separately adds the diffeomorphism condition for a canonical transformation. The shear additionally is a smooth global diffeomorphism, with inverse (Q,P) maps to (Q,P+lambda Q); direct multiplication gives J. The claimed counterexample distinguishes transformations from maps and does not refute F2 or the Example.

The published smooth Hamiltonian-field existence/uniqueness theorem is explicitly restated in the division-of-labour bullet but absent from deps. Its actual Statement is the unique smooth solution of iota_X omega=dH on a symplectic manifold for smooth H, matching the restatement. Added that theorem to deps and dependency_roles and synchronized the owned manifest row under the shared lock. This is a nonfatal omitted dependency declaration; mathematical prose and all supplier Statements remain unchanged.

The integration constant in hat S(theta,P)=theta P+mP+c(theta) is necessarily c(theta)=hat S(theta,0), by evaluating at P=0. Since the lifted S is 1-periodic in theta at every fixed P, it follows at P=0 that c(1)=c(0). The other generating relation gives c prime=-1 and hence c(1)-c(0)=-1, a valid contradiction. Periodicity at general P also gives c(1)-c(0)=-P, yielding another incompatibility, and does not negate periodicity at P=0. Checked local mixed derivative 1 and the loop integral 1; no item edit is needed.
